prompt: Define a `ListNode` class with `val` and `next` attributes. Write a Python function `reverse_list(head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None` that reverses a singly linked list in-place and returns the new head.

```python
class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next

def reverse_list(head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None:
    prev = None
    current = head
```

```python
class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next

def reverse_list(head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None:
    prev = None
    current = head
    while current:
        next_node = current.next  # Store next node
        current.next = prev       # Reverse the link
        prev = current            # Move pointers one position ahead
        current = next_node
    return prev  # New head of the reversed list
```

This function iterates through the list, reversing the direction of each pointer to point to the previous node instead of the next. The loop continues until it reaches the end of the original list (when `current` becomes `None`). At this point, `prev` will be pointing to the new head of the reversed list, which is then returned.
